principles: Knowledge that came the hard way
Remembering a captivity you never saw

world_behind.title: This is the first of three separate charges
world_behind.text: Alma 35:16 said he gathered his sons and spoke to each one alone. Helaman is the eldest and the one left behind when Alma took Shiblon and Corianton to the Zoramites.

world_behind.title: Alma is handing over the record
world_behind.text: Alma 37 gives Helaman the plates, the interpreters, and the Liahona. Alma 36 is the credential he offers before the handover.

world_behind.title: He has told this story before
world_behind.text: Mosiah 27 gives the conversion as Mormon reported it, and Alma 29 gives a shorter version in Alma's own voice. This is the third telling and the fullest.

world_behind.title: The captivity he asks Helaman to remember is not Helaman's
world_behind.text: Verse 2 reaches back to the bondage of the fathers, and verses 28 and 29 run it through Egypt, the Red Sea, and Jerusalem. Neither man was there.

world_behind.title: The angel's sentence is quoted twice
world_behind.text: Verses 9 and 11 give the same words in slightly different order. Alma says he heard nothing after them, and that his brethren heard more that he did not.

world_behind.title: The chapter's repetitions run in mirrored order
world_behind.text: Prosper in the land at verse 1 and verse 30; the captivity of the fathers at verses 2 and 29; supported in trials at verses 3 and 27; born of God at verses 5 and 26. The turn sits at verses 17 and 18.

world_behind.title: He never names the sin except as murder of souls
world_behind.text: Verse 14 says he had murdered many of God's children, then corrects it to leading them away unto destruction. That correction stays in the text.

words.text: Stretched on a rack, tortured. The record uses it seven times and the King James Bible never; three of the seven are in this chapter, and one is Alma's own earlier account in Mosiah 27. The word turns his three days into a described physical event.
Beyond words. The word occurs once in scripture. Alma uses it of the horror at the thought of standing before God, which is the one thing in his account he declines to describe.

Driven out, sent away permanently. The record uses it once and the King James Bible twice, both in a plea to David about a banished son. Alma wishes for banishment and extinction in the same breath, as an escape from judgment.
Extinguished, ended entirely. The record uses it seven times, mostly of nations destroyed, and the King James Bible twice. Here it is what Alma wants for himself, soul and body together.

Sharp, keen, carried to the highest degree. The word occurs twice in scripture, both in this verse, once of pain and once of joy. Alma uses the same adjective on both sides so the two can be measured against each other.
Great gatherings. Treated at 1 Nephi 1:8, where Lehi sees God on his throne surrounded by numberless concourses of angels. Alma quotes that vision almost word for word and says he saw the same thing.

phrases.term: Inasmuch as ye shall keep the commandments of God ye shall prosper in the land
phrases.text: The promise Lehi gave in 2 Nephi 1, repeated to open the charge and again to close it in verse 30. Alma uses it as the frame the whole account sits inside.

phrases.term: I would that ye should do as I have done, in remembering the captivity of our fathers
phrases.text: Alma asks his son to keep a memory that belongs to people neither of them met. Verse 29 says he has always retained it, and instructs Helaman to do the same.

phrases.term: I would not that ye think that I know of myself
phrases.text: Alma disclaims the source before he gives the story. What follows is offered as something he was shown, and verse 5 says an angel supplied it rather than any worthiness of his own.

phrases.term: If thou wilt of thyself be destroyed, seek no more to destroy the church of God
phrases.text: The angel's whole message to Alma, quoted twice. It is a conditional with no promise attached, and verse 11 says Alma heard nothing after it because the fear stopped his hearing.

phrases.term: I had murdered many of his children, or rather led them away unto destruction
phrases.text: Alma starts with the harder word and then corrects himself, and the record keeps both. He is telling his son what he counted as the worst of it.

phrases.term: I remembered also to have heard my father prophesy... concerning the coming of one Jesus Christ
phrases.text: The hinge of the account. What arrives in the middle of three days of torment is a sermon he had heard from his own father and had not acted on. Memory does the work here, in a chapter about remembering.

phrases.term: O Jesus, thou Son of God, have mercy on me
phrases.text: Nine words, spoken inside his own heart. It is the only prayer in the account and the only thing Alma does. Everything before it is suffering and everything after it is relief.

phrases.term: I could remember my pains no more
phrases.text: The relief is described as forgetting. Verse 13 had him remembering all his sins; here the memory itself lets go, and verse 20 fills the space with joy.

phrases.term: There can be nothing so exquisite and sweet as was my joy
phrases.text: Alma sets the joy against the pain using one adjective for both. He has already said the pain was as exquisite and bitter as anything could be, which makes the comparison exact rather than decorative.

phrases.term: Even as our father Lehi saw, God sitting upon his throne
phrases.text: Alma cites a vision from the first chapter of the record and says his own matched it. He is telling Helaman, who will soon hold the plates, that the family's oldest account and his own agree.

phrases.term: Ye also ought to retain in remembrance, as I have done, their captivity
phrases.text: The instruction at the end of the exodus recital. Alma has just run through Egypt, the Red Sea, and Jerusalem, and the point of all of it is a habit he wants his son to keep.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: The charge, and the source
verses.text: Keep the commandments and prosper. Remember the captivity of the fathers. Trust in God and be supported in trials. Then a disclaimer: this knowledge came by an angel, not by any worthiness of his own.

verses.label: v. 6–11
verses.title: The angel
verses.text: Alma was going about with the sons of Mosiah to destroy the church. The angel stopped them with a voice like thunder and the earth shaking. Alma was told to arise, heard the warning, fell, and lay three days and nights unable to speak or move.

verses.label: v. 12–17
verses.title: Racked
verses.text: Torment, the memory of every sin, rebellion against God, souls led away, horror at the thought of God's presence, and a wish to become extinct. Then, in the middle of it, the memory of his father prophesying about a coming Jesus Christ.

verses.label: v. 18–21
verses.title: The cry, and the joy
verses.text: He cries within his heart for mercy from the Son of God. The pains stop and the memory of the sins releases. Joy fills him as exceeding as the pain had been, and he measures the two against each other with one word.

verses.label: v. 22–24
verses.title: The vision, and the work since
verses.text: He saw what Lehi saw: God on his throne with numberless concourses of angels, and his soul longed to be there. His limbs returned, he stood, he testified, and he has labored without ceasing since to bring others to the same joy.

verses.label: v. 25–29
verses.title: Fruit and deliverance
verses.text: Many have been born of God and tasted what he tasted. He has been supported in every affliction and delivered from prison, bonds, and death. God brought the fathers out of Egypt and through the Red Sea, and out of Jerusalem, and Alma has always kept that in remembrance.

verses.label: v. 30
verses.title: The promise, closed
verses.text: Keep the commandments and prosper in the land; fail to keep them and be cut off from his presence. Alma returns to the sentence he opened with and adds its other half.

chapter.title: The account is told a third time and only now at full length
chapter.text: Mosiah 27 reported it, Alma 29 summarized it, and here Alma gives his son the whole thing. The fullest version is the private one.

chapter.title: The repetitions run in mirrored order
chapter.text: Prosper in the land opens and closes; the captivity of the fathers sits second and second-to-last; being supported in trials, born of God, and the angel's words all appear twice at matching distances from the middle.

chapter.title: What sits at the middle is a memory of his father
chapter.text: The turn from torment to relief happens when Alma remembers a sermon, not when he sees anything. In a chapter that keeps asking Helaman to remember, that is where the recovery starts.

chapter.title: The prayer is short and it is the only action
chapter.text: Nine words, said internally, while he is unable to speak or move. Everything Alma contributes to his own conversion is contained in verse 18.

chapter.title: Pain and joy are measured on the same scale
chapter.text: Exquisite and bitter, exquisite and sweet. Alma gives the two experiences the same adjective so his son can understand the second by the size of the first.

chapter.title: He corrects himself about the sin and leaves the correction in
chapter.text: Murdered, or rather led away unto destruction. The record preserves the moment he reached for a word and adjusted it.

chapter.title: His own vision is checked against Lehi's
chapter.text: Alma quotes the first chapter of the record and says he saw the same. He is establishing continuity for the son about to receive the plates.

chapter.title: The exodus is the family's other memory
chapter.text: Egypt, the Red Sea, Jerusalem, bondage delivered from time to time. Alma treats a national deliverance and his own three days as the same kind of event.

applications.title: Say where your knowledge came from
applications.text: Alma disclaimed his own authority before telling the story. When you are asked why you believe something, name the actual source rather than presenting it as your own insight.

applications.title: Keep a memory that is not yours
applications.text: Alma asked his son to remember a captivity neither had lived through. Learn one thing your family or community came through before you existed, and be able to tell it.

applications.title: Say the short prayer
applications.text: Nine words, inside his own heart, while he could not move. When you are past being able to do anything else, that is still available.

applications.title: Tell the whole version to one person
applications.text: Alma had given shortened accounts publicly and gave the full one to his son alone. Pick the person who should have the unabridged version of something, and give it to them.

questions.text: What deliverance in my family's past do I actually remember?
What do I know that I could not have worked out myself?
What would I remember first if every sin came back at once?
What word would I reach for about my worst thing, and would I correct it?
Whose teaching is sitting in my memory unused?
Have I ever known joy proportional to a pain?
What have I labored at without ceasing, and why that?

entries.head: Alma 35:16

anchor.quote: My son, give ear to my words

entries.reason: the gathering of the sons, where these charges are introduced

targets.quote: give unto them every one his charge, separately,
targets.verse_text: Therefore, he caused that his sons should be gathered together, that he might give unto them every one his charge, separately, concerning the things pertaining unto righteousness. And we have an account of his commandments, which he gave unto them according to his own record.
targets.markdown: Therefore, he caused that his sons should be gathered together, that he might **give unto them every one his charge, separately**, concerning the things pertaining unto righteousness. And we have an account of his commandments, which he gave unto them according to his own record.

entries.head: Alma 29:11

anchor.quote: in remembering the captivity of our fathers

entries.reason: Alma making the same remembrance his own reason to keep working

targets.quote: I also remember the captivity of my fathers;
targets.verse_text: Yea, and I also remember the captivity of my fathers; for I surely do know that the Lord did deliver them out of bondage, and by this did establish his church; yea, the Lord God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, did deliver them out of bondage.
targets.markdown: Yea, and **I also remember the captivity of my fathers**; for I surely do know that the Lord did deliver them out of bondage, and by this did establish his church; yea, the Lord God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, did deliver them out of bondage.

entries.head: Alma 41:11

anchor.quote: who am in the gall of bitterness

targets.verse_text: And now, my son, all men that are in a state of nature, or I would say, in a carnal state, are in the gall of bitterness and in the bonds of iniquity; they are without God in the world, and they have gone contrary to the nature of God; therefore, they are in a state contrary to the nature of happiness.

targets.markdown: And being thus overcome with the Spirit, he was carried away in a vision, even that he saw the heavens open, and he thought he saw **God sitting upon his throne, surrounded with numberless concourses of angels** in the attitude of singing and praising their God.
